source.publication: 2025 Form CT-1040 Instructions (Rev. 12/25) and Form CT-1040
source.section: PDF page 8, Schedule 1 Line 41 (MFJ, Line 1 less than 100,000: enter federally taxable benefits); PDF page 24, Social Security Benefit Adjustment Worksheet first questions; PDF pages 19-23, Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 1-10 with Table A, Table B, Tables C-D and Table E; Form CT-1040 Lines 1-6

worked: Federal AGI = wages 55,000.00 + taxable Social Security 25,500.00 (of 30,000.00 gross, federal worksheet) = 80,500.00. Federal taxable income = 80,500.00 - 31,500.00 standard deduction - 1 x 1,600.00 age 65+ = 47,400.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). CT-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 80,500.00; Line 2 additions 0.00 (Schedule 1 Lines 31-37: none apply); Line 3 = 80,500.00. Schedule 1 Line 41 Social Security benefit adjustment: federal AGI 80,500.00 is less than 100,000.00, so the full federally taxable amount 25,500.00 is subtracted (ss_full_exempt) -> 25,500.00. Schedule 1 Line 50 total subtractions = 25,500.00; CT-1040 Line 4 = 25,500.00. CT-1040 Line 5 Connecticut AGI = 80,500.00 - 25,500.00 = 55,000.00. Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1 = 55,000.00; Line 2 Table A: Connecticut AGI 55,000.00 is more than 54,000.00, exemption 17,000.00; Line 3 taxable income = 55,000.00 - 17,000.00 = 38,000.00. Line 4 Table B (Married Filing Jointly/Qualifying Surviving Spouse schedule) on 38,000.00: 20,000.00 x 0.02 + 18,000.00 x 0.045 = 400.00 + 810.00 = 1,210.00. Line 5 Table C 0.00 (Connecticut AGI 55,000.00 is not more than 100,500.00); Line 6 Table D 0.00 (not more than 210,000.00); Line 7 = 1,210.00. Line 8 Table E decimal 0.10 (Connecticut AGI 55,000.00 is in the band more than 52,000.00); Line 9 = 1,210.00 x 0.10 = 121.00. Line 10 Connecticut income tax = 1,210.00 - 121.00 = 1,089.00 (CT-1040 Line 6). No other credits (property tax credit not claimed: no property tax in the inputs, and not modelled).
